title: Clean a Messy Synthetic IS Table
prompt: Given raw_df with columns 'sku' (whitespace/lowercase) and 'qty' (strings including 'bad'), clean 'sku' with .str.strip().str.upper(), convert 'qty' with pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce'), drop rows where 'qty' is NaN, and drop duplicate 'sku' rows into clean_df.
solution:
import pandas as pd
raw_df = pd.DataFrame({'sku': [' a1 ', 'A1', 'b2'], 'qty': ['5', '5', 'bad']})
raw_df['sku'] = raw_df['sku'].str.strip().str.upper()
raw_df['qty'] = pd.to_numeric(raw_df['qty'], errors='coerce')
clean_df = raw_df.dropna(subset=['qty']).drop_duplicates(subset=['sku'])
explanation: Normalizing strings before drop_duplicates ensures ' a1 ' and 'A1' are recognized as duplicates.

title: pd.to_numeric errors='coerce'
solution: Converts unparseable strings to NaN instead of raising ValueError.
front: What does `pd.to_numeric(s, errors="coerce")` do when it encounters `'N/A'`?
back: It converts invalid/unparseable values into `NaN` instead of raising an error.
